title: Release Windows Playbook for Staggered Rollouts: Runtime, Console, and API
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Purpose: establish a single playbook for scheduling and executing staggered release windows across the Runtime, Console, and Public API surfaces. This ticket codifies windows, gating criteria, rollbacks, and communications so teams can safely coordinate multi-surface launches without blocking fast iteration.

Scope: runtime binary/service updates, console UI/feature rollouts, API contract changes (including deprecations), and telemetry/feature-flag gating. Not in scope: deep infra scaling projects that span multiple quarters (those get separate release plans).

Goals: unify cadence; reduce cross-team release collisions; define predictable blackout and high-risk windows; create a lightweight approval matrix; ensure rollback and canary steps are automated where possible; track OKRs and post-launch regressions in a single dashboard.
updates: 2025-02-12: Initial outline shared with Eng/SRE/Design for feedback. Requested examples of last-quarter collision incidents (SRE provided two).

2025-02-20: PM/Eng sync — agreed on three standard release windows (US morning, EU morning, APAC evening) and two blackout ranges per quarter. Eng requested explicit autoscale test before large runtime releases.
2025-02-27: Design provided UI copy guidance for console feature flags and rollout indicators. Added UX checklist to gating criteria.
2025-03-03: Security reviewed API contract changes process; we decided to require an opt-in deprecation notice 90 days before any breaking change. Noted as dependency for API teams.
2025-03-10: Draft playbook uploaded to /confluence/release-playbooks/release-windows-playbook. SRE asked for a runbook snippet for emergency rollback — added to 'roles' and 'gating_criteria'.
2025-03-12: Leadership requested that Dedicated (customer) impact be flagged for any runtime releases that change SLAs — added to metrics and acceptance criteria.
roles: Release Owner: PM (Lena Park) — approves window and coordinates stakeholders
SRE Lead: owns canary & rollback automation (TBD - ENG) — executes emergency rollback
Runtime Eng Lead: validates kernel/runtime compatibility and capacity reservations
Console Eng Lead: verifies UI feature-flag behavior and telemetry
API Product Lead: signs off on contract changes and deprecation notices
Design Liaison: reviews UX for feature flag state and user communications
Customer Success Rep: prepares high-touch customers for changes when necessary
gating_criteria: Automated canary for 15 minutes with baseline KPIs (latency, error-rate, p99) within threshold
No open P0/P1 incidents across affected services in 48 hours prior to window
Rollout plan documented with rollback steps and an identified SRE/ENG on-call
Telemetry and tracing hooks validated in preprod and smoke-tested in staging
API: deprecation notices published 90 days prior for breaking changes and client compatibility tests green
Console: UX acceptance tests & accessibility checks passed
Dedicated/Private customers: communication sent 7 business days before window if SLA or config changes
rollout_windows: Window A (US Morning): 08:00-11:00 PST — primary for non-breaking runtime and console features; low-latency expectation for US customers
Window B (EU Morning): 09:00-12:00 CET — used for region-targeted console/API changes and cross-region runtime adjustments
Window C (APAC Evening): 17:00-20:00 JST/AEDT — preferred for APAC-focused experiments and low-risk API releases
Canary cohort: 1% traffic for 15 minutes -> 5% for 30 minutes -> 25% for 2 hours -> 100% if stable
Emergency/Hotfix window: ad-hoc, requires Release Owner + SRE lead approval; must include post-mortem within 72 hours
communication_plan: Pre-window: announcement in #release-orchestration and targeted customer email (if impacted) 72/48/24 hours. During-window: live status updates in Slack thread and a minimal change log entry. Post-window: summary in Confluence and retrospective in the next weekly release meeting. Any rollback triggers must be announced within 5 minutes to execs and customer success for high-impact incidents.
risks: Peak traffic in a region coincides with a planned window — mitigation: prefer off-peak windows and optional shift by 2 hours
Interdependent changes across surfaces (runtime + API + console) create combinatorial risk — mitigation: require explicit cross-team sign-off and separate canary cohorts
Insufficient telemetry coverage for a change — mitigation: pre-window instrumentation checklist mandatory
Dedicated customer environments lag behind hosted rollout — mitigation: customer-specific runbook and opt-in testing cohort
okrs: O1: Reduce release-related cross-team incidents by 40% this quarter — KR1: enforce the playbook for 100% of coordinated releases
O2: Improve mean time to detect (MTTD) for rollout regressions by 30% — KR1: standardize canary KPIs and dashboards for all releases
O3: Decrease time-to-serve for staged rollouts from decision to production by 20% — KR1: automate approval gating for low-risk changes
metrics: canary-pass-rate (percent of releases passing canary without manual intervention)
time from window start to full rollout (hours)
acceptance_criteria: Playbook doc reviewed and approved by Eng, SRE, Design, Security, and CS
Release windows template and calendar entries created and published for Q2
Automated canary job and rollback script checked into release-scripts with at least one successful dry-run in staging
OKR metrics dashboard created and linked from the playbook
Training session scheduled for on-call and release owners (recording uploaded to Drive)
